scope.purpose: Supplement federal snapshot with reliably documented later casualty events, without claiming exhaustive coverage.

additionalCases.place: 1000 block of West Venice Boulevard, Pico-Union, near Toberman Street
additionalCases.shortSummary: A sedan and a Waymo collided on Venice Boulevard. Fire officials reported two people hospitalized and another treated at the scene.
additionalCases.causeSummary: Waymo says the other car struck a pedestrian before entering the opposite lane and hitting its vehicle. Police said their investigation was ongoing.
additionalCases.causalClassification: AV involved; independent fault determination unavailable
additionalCases.causationLimits: Counts cover the entire crash sequence. The pedestrian may have been injured by the sedan before it hit the Waymo. Public evidence does not assign particular injuries to AV action.
additionalCases.engagementEvidence: Original TV reporting describes an autonomous Waymo; company supplied a 27 mph travel speed and collision sequence. No operator filing confirming exact ADS-at-impact status was reviewed.
additionalCases.adsEngagementStatus: reported autonomous; exact status not independently established in reviewed sources
additionalCases.countExplanation: NBC4 quotes LAFD for three injuries, including two transported and a young person treated/released. ABC7 quotes LAPD for a critically injured woman and four others with pain; details and totals differ across outlets. Use at least 3 rather than silently choosing a supposedly exact total.

sources.title: NBC4: Two-vehicle crash involving Waymo leaves 3 injured near downtown LA
sources.evidence: Original reporting quoting LAFD and LAPD; three injured, two hospitalized.

sources.title: ABC7: Woman critically injured in 2-car crash involving Waymo vehicle in Southern California
sources.evidence: Original reporting quotes LAPD for one woman hospitalized and four others treated for pain; provides company statement on collision sequence.

additionalCases.duplicateHandling: Event after federal July15 reporting cutoff; do not merge its distinct July26 Atlanta event. Future federal reports must be matched by date/place and deduplicated.
additionalCases.readerNote: NBC4 reported three injuries, while ABC7 reported five. This entry counts at least three. News reports describe an autonomous Waymo; driving mode at impact is not independently confirmed in the reviewed federal records.

additionalCases.place: Cheshire Bridge Road near Manchester Street
additionalCases.shortSummary: A Jeep rear-ended an empty Waymo and a fire followed. One Jeep occupant suffered burns; another reported a shoulder injury.
additionalCases.causeSummary: Firefighters described the Jeep striking the Waymo from behind. Waymo says its vehicle was making a left turn; no final fault finding was located.
additionalCases.causalClassification: AV involved; rear-ended by another vehicle, no final fault finding located
additionalCases.causationLimits: Both injured people were in the Jeep. Do not label them casualties caused by the AV solely because it was involved.
additionalCases.engagementEvidence: FOX5 and WSB describe the unoccupied vehicle as driverless; Waymo supplied its vehicle movement and collision data.
additionalCases.adsEngagementStatus: driverless operation reported by original news sources and company statement
additionalCases.countExplanation: FOX5 original reporting quotes Atlanta Fire Rescue Capt. Andrew Anderson and explicitly describes burns and a shoulder injury. WSB reports two evaluated and declined hospital transport.

sources.title: FOX5 Atlanta: 2 hurt after Waymo driverless car catches fire in Atlanta
sources.evidence: Original reporting quoting Atlanta Fire Rescue; describes two specific injuries.

sources.title: WSB-TV: Waymo catches fire after car crashes into back of it
sources.evidence: Two evaluated in other vehicle, declined hospital transport; empty Waymo rear-ended according to company.

additionalCases.duplicateHandling: Event after federal July15 reporting cutoff; distinct from July26 Los Angeles collision. Match future reports by date/place before adding.
additionalCases.readerNote: The two specifically described injuries were in the Jeep. The Waymo was reported to be unoccupied.

existingCaseVerified.shortSummary: An SUV hit a pedestrian, throwing him into a Waymo coming the other way. He died after being taken to hospital.
existingCaseVerified.causeSummary: Dallas police described the SUV as the first vehicle to strike him. The empty Waymo was also involved; this source does not establish that the AV caused the death.
existingCaseVerified.causalClassification: AV involved; pedestrian initially struck by human-driven SUV
existingCaseVerified.engagementEvidence: FOX4 reports the moving Waymo was unoccupied.

source.title: FOX4 Dallas-Fort Worth: Dallas pedestrian dies after being struck by SUV, thrown into Waymo

existingCaseVerified.duplicateHandling: Already known to parent; verify/update existing case only, do not add twice.

notAdded.place: Denver, West 8th Avenue and Delaware Street
notAdded.reason: 9News and Westword say people were evaluated and no serious injuries, without establishing a positive injury count. Evaluation alone cannot become an injured person.
notAdded.causationNote: Westword quotes DPD: initial driver cited for following too closely; no indication Waymo caused crash.

notAdded.reason: Social media and Citizen injury references surfaced, but no verified casualty total or authoritative/original news report located. Excluded from casualty marks.
Workers allege continued 2026 injuries; incident dates and counts unavailable.
August reporting concerns previously known January child collision, already federal report 30270-13850; not a new August event.

limits: This is a bounded search of public reporting, not an exhaustive police or regulator census.
News publication date was not treated as incident date.
Only positive casualty evidence produced added marks; unknown counts were not converted to zero.
Involvement is not causation. Counts cover crash sequences and can overlap with human-driven crashes.
No documented federal record ID was available for the two added July26 events; later updates need deduplication.
Non-collision worker injuries may be missing from federal crash reporting and cannot be counted from undated testimony.
